details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of severe wind gusts and hail will increase from west to east during the next few hours. A watch may be needed relatively soon for parts of the area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated high-based thunderstorms are evolving along a lee trough extending from the NE Panhandle southward into northeastern CO, and storm coverage should continue to increase as a subtle midlevel wave approaches the area from the west (per recent WV loops). Over the next few hours, this activity will spread eastward into a a plume of middle/upper 50s dewpoints and steep deep-layer lapse rates, which are contributing to a moderately unstable air mass. This, combined with an elongating and mostly straight hodograph, should support some convective organization/cell splitting. While severe hail will be possible (especially in the earlier stages of convective intensification), the primary concern will be an increasing risk of severe wind gusts with any clustering that occurs. A watch may be needed relatively soon for parts of the area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: So far this afternoon, thunderstorms in southeast NY and eastern PA have remained disorganized within a broader band of lower reflectivity, presumably due to poor lapse rate profiles. Ahead of the ongoing storms, temperatures have warmed into the mid 80s to lower 90s with latest objective analysis indicating a corridor of steeper low-level lapse rates, which may support some storm organization into early evening, given the presence of 35-40 kt of westerly deep-layer shear

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for damaging wind gusts may increase through late afternoon as the ongoing storms encounter a more unstable air mass

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Strong to potentially severe storms currently emerging from the Blue Ridge Mountains are moving into a hotter and more unstable air mass, characterized by MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg and 0-3 km lapse rates of around 8 C/km. Moreover, The KLWX VWP is sampling strengthening westerly winds above 3.5 km AGL, which may aid in storm organization. The extent of the damaging wind threat will be dependent on the degree of cold-pool organization that can occur. However, the more favorable parameter space with eastward extent suggests that threat should increase through late afternoon
